dedupe_keys.name: cycles and cycles l agroecosystem models penn state

description: Cycles is a process-based agroecosystem model that simulates agricultural productivity, as grain, forage and biomass yield, and the water, carbon and nitrogen balance of soil-crop systems under climate, soil and management constraints. It is multi-year, multi-crop, multi-layer and one-dimensional, runs at daily or sub-daily steps, and takes initial soil properties, daily weather and management such as crop sequence, fertiliser rates and timing, irrigation and tillage; many modules relate to CropSyst. Cycles-L extends it to watersheds with water and nutrient transport through surface, groundwater and streams. It was developed by Armen Kemanian, Charlie White, Yuning Shi and Claudio Stöckle at Penn State's Agroecosystems Modeling Laboratory, with Lorne Leonard as software architect. Coverage is generic for any site with the inputs. The model is available free through a Penn State site, a user's guide and releases on GitHub; the page read does not state a licence. Caveats: it is one-dimensional at field scale, results depend on calibration, and the main model link was under maintenance at access. For simulation it estimates how droughts, heat and management changes affect yields and nutrient losses, supporting climate adaptation and water quality studies of farm systems. It is related to the DSSAT cropping system model record in this catalogue.
